items.title: Switching costs create lock-in even without monopoly
items.claim: Mobile phone contracts, banking services and software subscriptions all create switching costs. How does this affect competition?

options.text: High switching costs reduce price elasticity, allow price discrimination, and create incumbency advantages; competition can shift from price-on-price to acquisition incentives that don't always benefit existing customers
Switching costs only exist in monopoly

items.reveal:
Klemperer's research (1987 onwards) formalised switching cost economics. UK's Open Banking initiative (2018), CASS (Current Account Switch Service 2013) and Ofcom's text-to-switch (2019) all aim to reduce switching frictions specifically.

The CMA's 2016 retail banking market investigation found switching costs and informational frictions sustained higher prices and weak competition.
items.why: Competition exists on a spectrum shaped by frictions. Policy can target the frictions directly (lower switching costs) rather than only firm conduct.

items.title: US tariffs on China were largely absorbed by US importers
items.claim: Amiti, Redding and Weinstein (Journal of Economic Perspectives, 2019) studied the incidence of 2018 US tariffs on Chinese imports. What did they find?

options.text: Chinese exporters paid the entire tariff
Nearly the full cost of the tariffs was passed through to US importers and consumers; producer prices in China barely changed. The 'tariffs hurt foreigners' framing did not match the price data

items.reveal:
Amiti, Redding and Weinstein analysed customs and price data through 2019. The pass-through was nearly complete to US importers; Chinese export prices for affected goods didn't drop substantially.

Fajgelbaum, Goldberg, Kennedy and Khandelwal (QJE 2020) confirmed the finding using different methods. Subsequent Biden-era tariffs (2024) followed similar patterns. The US-China tariffs reshaped supply chains (Vietnam, Mexico saw substantial increases in exports to the US) more than they raised significant revenue.
items.why: The political rhetoric of tariffs often diverges from the economic incidence. Trade policy effects are empirically measurable; the empirics often don't support the political framing.

items.title: The Bank of England became independent in 1997
items.claim: Gordon Brown announced operational independence for the Bank of England in May 1997, days after Labour's election victory. What's the standard rationale?

options.text: To allow politicians to set interest rates directly

To insulate monetary policy from short-term political pressure, given evidence that independent central banks (Bundesbank, Fed) had lower average inflation. The Treasury sets the target; the Bank sets rates

items.reveal:
Alesina and Summers (1993) had documented the inverse correlation between central bank independence and inflation across OECD countries. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's 1989 Act pioneered explicit inflation targeting.

UK target: 2% CPI from 2003 (RPIX 2.5% before). The MPC has 9 members, votes monthly. Brown's surprise announcement preceded the post-1997 inflation stability period.

Independence has been challenged in some quarters since 2010s rate decisions; the Bank's bond buying in autumn 2022 (LDI crisis) raised questions about coordination with Treasury.
items.why: Institutional design — who decides what, accountable to whom — is as much a part of macroeconomic policy as the decisions themselves.
